headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Pipecat’s shared-bus, multi-API defaults can amplify outputs from a non-runnable course repo into external services.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a non-runnable course repo with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly inject B. Profile B uses a shared bus and multiple transports/APIs, so if A’s content is manually copied into B, prompt-like text could be propagated. The bridge is not default and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF an operator copies text from agent_a materials into agent_b prompts or memory
IF agent_b consumes shared-bus messages without provenance filtering
mitigations: Disable shared-bus ingestion for untrusted text
Use a provenance tag on all copied course content
Keep agent_a materials in a separate workspace
Review any pasted instructions before running agent_b

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A has no network egress, but agent B has allowlisted egress and touches text, conversation state, and analytics. If both share a workspace or bus, A’s materials can flow into B and then out to third-party APIs. This is plausible in default Pipecat-style deployments, so the interaction is not safely isolated.
conditions: IF agent_a artifacts are placed in the same workspace or bus as agent_b
IF agent_b forwards conversation state or text to an allowlisted external API
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents
Restrict agent_b API calls to non-sensitive inputs
Turn off analytics/metrics for shared sessions
Redact text before it enters agent_b
requires-engineering: add per-message provenance and policy checks

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A exposes no write or network surfaces, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. Agent B supports multiple instances on a shared bus, which can create coordination issues, but the profile does not show overlapping filesystem or git writes. The conflict pathway is therefore limited and not clearly dangerous by default.
conditions: IF multiple agent_b instances write to the same shared bus state
IF an external orchestrator maps both agents onto the same mutable resource
mitigations: Assign separate session IDs
Avoid shared mutable state between instances
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Check for duplicate writers before launch

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B can treat text and conversation state as live inputs, and its many LLM/STT/TTS integrations make it likely to act on upstream content. Agent A is a course repo whose outputs may be copied into B as instructions or facts. Without a verification step, A’s content can cascade into B’s downstream actions or responses.
conditions: IF agent_a content is used as source material for agent_b prompts or memory
IF agent_b forwards unverified outputs into downstream APIs or user-facing responses
mitigations: Require human review before B acts on A-derived text
Add a verification step for citations and facts
Limit B to read-only summarization of A content
Log source provenance for every forwarded item
requires-engineering: enforce structured handoff contracts

E_compliance.rationale: Agent A is an open-source course repo with no touched data classes, while agent B handles audio, video, images, text, and conversation state and can egress to allowlisted services. No residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented, so only a general compliance gap exists if sensitive content is introduced into B.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through agent_b services
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the text/audio flowing through agent_b
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of agent_b
Document retention settings for each external API
Disable analytics on sensitive sessions
Use region-appropriate providers
requires-engineering: add a data-processing agreement review
